title.narrative: Angola Strengthening Governance for Enhanced Service Delivery Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Strengthening Governance for Enhanced Service Delivery Project for Angola is to increase the amount and reliability of fiscal transfers to selected municipalities; strengthen their public financial and land management capacity; and increase identity coverage. The project comprises of five components. The first component strengthened financial autonomy of selected municipalities through establishment of a municipal performance grant will support the establishment of a municipal performance grant (MPG) fund to incentivize selected municipalities to improve their public financial management (PFM) capacity, thus supporting an enabling environment for better delivery of administrative and public services. The second component, strengthening financial and land management capacity in selected municipalities objective is to strengthen capacity in PFM and urban land management systems. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthening central and subnational PFM capacity; and (ii) improving urban planning and land management in selected municipalities. The third component, increasing identity coverage to enable inclusive access to services objective is to increase identification coverage. The fourth component, project management will support the implementing institutions to achieve project results and provide just in time funds. The fifth component, contingency emergency response component (CERC) is included to facilitate access to rapid financing in the event of a natural disaster, either by a formal declaration of a national or regional emergency or upon a formal request.
To increase the amount and reliability of fiscal transfers to selected municipalities; strengthen their public financial and land management capacity; and increase identity coverage.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2 Section I D (PIU) The Borrower shall: (i) maintain throughout Project implementation, the PIU in charge of the overallimplementation, coordination and management of the Project, with adequate resources, responsibilities, and key staff under terms ofreference and qualification acceptable to the Bank, such staff to include: (a) a coordinator; (b) a procurement specialist; (c) afinancial management specialist; (ii) no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date hire or appoint and thereafter maintaina social development specialist; and (iii) no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date hire or appoint and thereaftermaintain: (a) an environment specialist; (b) a communications specialist; (c) a monitoring and evaluation specialist; and (d)technical and administrative personnel; all with terms of reference, qualification and experience satisfactory to the Bank and asfurther detailed in the POM.

Schedule 2 Section I E (Regional PIUs)The Borrower shall establish no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date andthereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, the Regional PIUs in charge of the implementation, coordination andmanagement of the Project at the regional level, with adequate resources, responsibilities, and key staff under terms of reference,qualification and experience acceptable to the Bank, such staff to include: (i) not later than three (3) months after the EffectiveDate a coordinator and two social specialists (to cover four Regional PIUs); and (ii) not later than five (5) months after theEffective Date, a procurement specialist; a financial management specialist; an environment specialist (to cover four RegionalPIUs); and administrative and technical personnel, as further detailed in the POM.

Schedule 2 Section II B (External Monitoring)The Borrower shall, not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, appointand thereafter maintain during the implementation of the Project, an independent third party, to carry out the oversight of andquarterly reporting on the operation and use of the identification systems being designed and implemented under Part 3 of theProject under terms of reference and with qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Bank.

Schedule 2 Section IV (Other Undertakings)Not later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, or any other such date agreedby the Bank, the Borrower shall prepare, consult upon, adopt and disclose the ESMF, the LMP, the WMP, the IPPF, the codes ofconduct and the grievance redress mechanisms for the Project in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.

title.narrative: Elaboration of climate-informed Municipal Master Plans (PDMs) in selected municipalities

comment.narrative:
Approval and official publication of PDMs
Status: Two procurement activities are underway for the preparation of Municipal Master Plans (PDMs) for six municipalities in the provinces of Luanda and Cuanza Sul (first activity) and six municipalities in the provinces of Huila and Cunene (second activity). The contract for the preparation of the PDMs for Maquela do Zombo and Bembe in Uige province were signed on January 8, 2025.

title.narrative: Implementation of SAGIT in selected municipalities

comment.narrative: At MTR, The Sistema Angolano de Gestão de Informação de Terras (SAGIT) has not been fully implemented in any project municipality. Project support to date has included acquisition of IT equipment and technical assistance to upgrade SAGIT. The project is reassessing the scope and sequencing of SAGIT implementation to support more realistic progress during the remaining implementation period.

title.narrative: Public financial management practices strengthened in municipalities

comment.narrative: Capacity-building on public financial management has been delivered at scale through ENAPP, with municipal staff in project municipalities trained on budgeting, execution reporting, and the use of national PFM systems. Municipalities are preparing budgets and budget execution reports using SIGFE, although implementation remains uneven, with partial electronic workflows and continued reliance on physical submission. These practices indicate progress in the adoption of SIGFE supported by project-financed training. Formal verification of municipal practices is ongoing by the Independent Verification Agent and will inform the reporting of this indicator.

title.narrative: Implementation of Citizens' Portal in target municipalities

comment.narrative:
Implementation of Citizens' Portal in target municipalities for the provision of services.
Status: Implementation of the Citizens' Portal precedes the implementation of the project. Notwithstanding, a set of relevant activities are included in the project's annual work plans for 2024 and 2025. This includes (a) the hiring of a firm to design the support structure (Service Desk) for the end user of the SNCPE/SIGFE/SIPIP systems and the Citizens' Portal, and (b) the adaptation of training content on the theoretical component and the use of the SNCPE/SIGFE/SIPIP systems and the Citizens' Portal. In terms of the first activity, the firm has already commended the work. As for the second activity, it is in the evaluation of expression of interest and shortlist of consultants phase.

title.narrative: Implementation of SAGIT in selected municipalities

comment.narrative:
SAGIT fully functional as per agreed specifications
Status: With respect to the implementation of SAGIT, two procurement activities are underway to (i) acquire IT equipment to support the national data center for SAGIT, and (ii) hire a firm for the development of new functionalities of SAGIT and its manual for 12 Municipalities. The first activity is at the Bid Evaluation Report and Recommendation for Award stage. As for the second activity, the Terms of Reference are being reviewed by the Bank team.

title.narrative: Municipalities demonstrating strengthened capacity for managing Municipal Performance Grants

comment.narrative: The Operational Manual for Component 1 was approved in June 2025, enabling the rollout of Municipal Performance Grants in 52 municipalities aligned with the new Political-Administrative Division. A portfolio of 212 municipal subprojects was identified through participatory processes involving Community Consultation Councils, and implementation is underway. As of the Mid-Term Review in February 2026, approximately 45 percent of the smaller grant-financed subprojects had been completed, while larger investment projects had only recently begun. An Independent Verification Agent has been recruited and is currently verifying achievement of the Performance-Based Conditions and the use of grant resources, which is required before progress under this indicator can be formally recognized.

title.narrative: Number of participants in the participatory cadaster process conducted in the priority municipalities

comment.narrative:
Number of people who attend information sessions related to the cadaster process and/or participate in the field work aspects of the cadaster process.
Status: The participatory cadaster process has not started yet. A consulting firm is being hired to design the Registration System and Cadaster for Residents' Committees and Councils.

As of the Mid-Term Review, procurement practices were assessed as enhanced in 13 municipalities, reflecting those currently using the National Electronic Public Procurement System (SNCPE), compared to 12 municipalities confirmed in the baseline study. Progress to date has been supported by extensive capacity-building activities delivered by ENAPP, which have trained municipal staff in public procurement and related areas across the project municipalities. While training coverage is strong, expansion of SNCPE use remains slower than expected due to pending certification of the system and delays in the provision of essential IT equipment. Contracts and procurement processes are underway to address these constraints and support broader adoption of e-procurement in additional municipalities.

title.narrative: Number of participants in the participatory cadaster process conducted in the priority municipalities

comment.narrative: The PIU reported that 20,021 people have participated in participatory cadaster process in priority municipalities, reaching 50% of the midterm target. Midterm proposed reevaluation of the end-target.

The current value of 48 reflects municipalities with Component 1 subprojects (PIP and DAD) registered in SIGFE, which is the basis used in the project's results framework to track municipalities receiving Municipal Performance Grants. Following approval of the Component 1 Operational Manual, implementation advanced through a portfolio of municipal subprojects, with smaller Development Support Expenditure activities progressing more rapidly, while Public Investment Projects only recently received authorization to commence execution. Verification by the Independent Verification Agent is ongoing to confirm compliance with the Performance-Based Conditions and the eligibility of expenditures, which remains critical for formal validation and documentation of results.

title.narrative: Implementation of Citizens' Portal in target municipalities

comment.narrative: Citizens Portal was rolled out to municipalities prior to the project, consequently, the mission recognized the need to revise the indicator to report usage and services available. Project support has focused strengthening use of the Portal, including through complementary capacity-building and planned investments in equipment and systems integration. This indicator will be reviewed for potential tracking under the CRI.

title.narrative: Number of civil registration posts renovated or in new health facilities

comment.narrative:
Number of civil registration posts functioning in health facilities including existing posts that need to be renovated and new posts created.
Status: Three procurement activities are underway for the renovation of 120 civil registration posts and the acquisition of the corresponding IT equipment and furniture. The first civil registration post supported by the project opened at the General Hospital of Cuanza Sul on October 21, 2024.

title.narrative: Number of civil registration posts renovated or in new health facilities

comment.narrative: Seven (7) civil registration posts have been renovated or established in new health facilities. While this represents initial progress toward expanding access to civil registration services, implementation remains at an early stage relative to the end target, and further rollout is ongoing. Though the result is below the midterm target, renovations of civil registration posts in on track to achieve end-target.

title.narrative: Municipalities holding PFM training events for municipal level public servants

baseline.value: No PFM training events for municipal level public servants

target.value: Selected municipalities (58) had least 2 PFM training events

comment.narrative: 50 municipalities have held at least one public financial management training event for municipal-level public servants, primarily delivered through the ENAPP training program. These trainings covered core PFM topics, including budgeting, financial management, procurement, and decentralization, and were implemented at scale across project municipalities. Progress toward the end-of-project target is strong, with training delivery exceeding mid-term expectations. The focus going forward is on consolidating training coverage and supporting the application of acquired skills in day-to-day municipal financial management practices.

title.narrative: Municipalities holding consultations with citizens across the budget cycle

baseline.value: No guidelines exist for consultation with citizens across the budget cycle.

target.value: 30 target municipalities have held consultations over 2 years with citizens across the budget cycle using guidelines (at end of which at least 40% are female)

comment.narrative: 32 municipalities have conducted consultations with citizens during at least one stage of the municipal budget cycle, primarily through engagement with Community Consultation Councils (CACs). These consultations have focused mainly on budget identification and annual reporting, with more limited use during budget execution and feedback stages. Ongoing capacity-building for CACs and planned follow-up actions are expected to support more consistent and structured citizen engagement during the remaining implementation period.
